rationale: Asturian (Asturian-Leonese) is an Ibero-Romance language of the West Iberian group. ISO 639-5: roa (Romance languages) under ine (Indo-European).
Faroese is a North Germanic language spoken in the Faroe Islands, closely related to Icelandic and Old Norse. ISO 639-5: gem (Germanic languages).

Limburgish (Limburgan/Limburgs) is a Low Franconian Germanic language spoken in the Limburg region. Misclassified as Romance in earlier reference data; corrected here. ISO 639-5: gem (Germanic languages).

Moldovan is a Romanian dialect used in Moldova. The ISO 639-1 code 'mo' is deprecated in favour of 'ro', but the Wikimedia language code persists for the distinct Wikipedia. ISO 639-5: roa (Romance languages).
Romansh (Rumantsch) is a Rhaeto-Romance language of the Swiss canton of Graubünden. ISO 639-5: roa (Romance languages).
Avestan is an ancient Eastern Iranian language used in Zoroastrian Avesta scripture. No longer spoken natively; included for completeness. ISO 639-5: ira (Iranian languages).
ISO 639-1 code 'bh' is a collective code for Bihari languages (Bhojpuri, Maithili, Magahi), all Eastern Indo-Aryan languages of Bihar. ISO 639-5: inc (Indic languages).
Dhivehi (Maldivian/Divehi) is an Indo-Aryan language of the Maldives and Lakshadweep, most closely related to Sinhala. ISO 639-5: inc (Indic languages).
Kashmiri is a Dardic language within the Indo-Aryan branch, spoken in the Kashmir Valley. ISO 639-5: inc (Indic languages).
Odia (Oriya) is an Eastern Indo-Aryan language of Odisha state, one of the classical languages of India. ISO 639-5: inc (Indic languages).
Pali is a Middle Indo-Aryan liturgical language and the canonical scriptural language of Theravada Buddhism. No longer a spoken vernacular. ISO 639-5: inc (Indic languages).
Romani is a Central Indo-Aryan language originating in the Indian subcontinent, spoken by Romani peoples across Europe and beyond. ISO 639-5: inc (Indic languages).
Sanskrit is the classical Old Indo-Aryan language and liturgical language of Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism. Still used in scholarship and ritual. ISO 639-5: inc (Indic languages).
Sindhi is a Northwestern Indo-Aryan language spoken primarily in Sindh (Pakistan) and parts of India. ISO 639-5: inc (Indic languages).
Sichuan Yi (Nuosu) is a Tibeto-Burman language of the Loloish (Ngwi) branch, spoken in Sichuan and Yunnan. ISO 639-5: sit (Sino-Tibetan languages).
Newari (Nepal Bhasa) is a Sino-Tibetan language of the Tibeto-Burman branch, spoken in the Kathmandu Valley by the Newar people. ISO 639-5: sit (Sino-Tibetan languages).

Zhuang (Standard Zhuang/Sawndip) is a Kra-Dai (Tai-Kadai) language of southern China, not Sino-Tibetan. Misclassified as Sino-Tibetan in earlier reference data; corrected here. ISO 639-5: tai (Tai languages).
Afar (Qafar af) is a Cushitic Afro-Asiatic language spoken in Djibouti, Ethiopia, and Eritrea. ISO 639-5: cus (Cushitic languages) under afa (Afro-Asiatic languages).
Herero (Otjiherero) is a Southern Bantu language of the Otjiherero-Himba group, spoken in Namibia and Botswana. ISO 639-5: bnt (Bantu languages) under nic (Niger-Kordofanian).
Kikuyu (Gĩkũyũ) is a Bantu language of the Central Kenya Bantu branch, the most widely spoken Bantu language in Kenya. ISO 639-5: bnt (Bantu languages).
Kuanyama (Oshikwanyama) is a dialect of Oshiwambo, a Southern Bantu language spoken in Namibia and Angola. ISO 639-5: bnt (Bantu languages).
Luba-Katanga (Kiluba) is a Central Bantu language of the Benue-Congo branch, spoken in Katanga province of the DRC. ISO 639-5: bnt (Bantu languages).
North Ndebele (isiNdebele) is a Southern Bantu Nguni language of Zimbabwe, closely related to Zulu. ISO 639-5: bnt (Bantu languages).
Ndonga (Oshindonga) is a dialect of Oshiwambo, a Southern Bantu language spoken in Namibia. ISO 639-5: bnt (Bantu languages).
South Ndebele (isiNdebele yeSewula) is a Southern Bantu Nguni language of South Africa, distinct from North Ndebele. ISO 639-5: bnt (Bantu languages).
Wolof is a Niger-Congo language of the Atlantic-Congo (Senegambian) branch, spoken primarily in Senegal, Gambia, and Mauritania. ISO 639-5: nic (Niger-Kordofanian languages).
Hiri Motu is a simplified pidgin/creole based on Motu (an Austronesian language), used as an administrative lingua franca in Papua New Guinea. ISO 639-5: crp (Creoles and pidgins).

Woods Cree (nêhiyawêwin) is a dialect of Cree, an Algonquian language of the Algic family spoken across northern Canada. ISO 639-5: alg (Algonquian languages) under nai (North American Indian languages).

Wolaytta (Wolayta) is an Omotic language of Ethiopia. Omotic is traditionally classified as a branch of Afro-Asiatic, though some linguists treat it as a separate family. ISO 639-5: afa (Afro-Asiatic languages) used as the closest available approximation.
